boundary: This registry describes SCRIMED's locally implemented, synthetic/no-PHI platform foundations and evidence paths. It does not authorize PHI, autonomous clinical care, diagnosis, treatment, prescribing, payer submission, EHR writeback, medical-device connectivity, production deployment, certification claims, customer activation, investor outreach, valuation claims, or revenue guarantees.
investorUse: Internal diligence preparation only; founder, finance, legal, and recipient-specific approval remain required for external distribution.

moatRegistry.name: Trust and governance plane
moatRegistry.basis: Policy-before-action, exact evidence binding, independent review, audit receipts, rollback, and release gates.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Each reviewed workflow contributes reusable policy, benchmark, failure, and approval evidence.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires integrated product, security, clinical, data, reviewer, and release controls rather than a prompt layer.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Supports governance assessments, protected pilots, and recurring enterprise control-plane subscriptions.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not prove certification, regulatory approval, customer adoption, or production safety.

moatRegistry.name: Healthcare evidence graph
moatRegistry.basis: FHIR, HL7, DICOM metadata, payer-policy, ontology, citation, and source-lineage contracts.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Validated mappings and source contracts improve retrieval, verification, and implementation reuse.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Depends on clinical semantics, tenant isolation, transformation lineage, and workflow-specific acceptance tests.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Improves diligence, implementation speed, grounding quality, and reusable evidence services.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not prove live EHR integration, medical-device interoperability, or standards certification.

moatRegistry.name: Longitudinal benchmark learning
moatRegistry.basis: Case evidence, accepted outcomes, corrections, worst-cell evaluation, reviewer burden, and value telemetry.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Reviewed failures become regression cases and workflow improvements without online clinical self-modification.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires longitudinal evidence and operator adoption, not merely access to the same model.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Can lower correction burden and strengthen renewal evidence once external outcomes are validated.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not establish causality, clinical outcomes, ROI, revenue, or customer traction before formal evidence.

moatRegistry.name: Multi-model routing
moatRegistry.basis: Provider-neutral routing, task qualification, no privacy downgrade, bounded fallback, and effective-cost accounting.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Per-task evidence improves model eligibility and cost choices while preserving replaceability.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires workflow-specific evaluation and policy-compatible failover across model and deployment classes.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Protects gross-margin scenarios and provider leverage without weakening privacy or safety floors.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not prove provider availability, BAA eligibility, PHI approval, or production-scale performance.

moatRegistry.name: Release assurance
moatRegistry.basis: Claims-safe offers, intended-use records, review packets, security gates, migration evidence, and controlled pilot operations.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Approved buyer and pilot evidence can shorten later diligence only when permission and scope remain current.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires trustworthy execution history with named owners and independent review.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Reduces enterprise diligence friction while keeping deployment and customer activation separately controlled.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not imply customers, partners, revenue, procurement approval, investment, or commercial deployment.

moatRegistry.name: Governed agent orchestration
moatRegistry.basis: Bounded planner-specialist-verifier execution with least privilege, checkpoints, approvals, cancellation, and rollback metadata.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Reusable policies, tool receipts, failure classes, and review patterns improve each governed workflow.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires orchestration, identity, policy, evidence, observability, and human operations to work as one system.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Enables repeatable workflow subscriptions and governed automation services.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not authorize autonomous clinical, financial, identity, communication, or production actions.

moatRegistry.name: Healthcare-specific evaluation corpus
moatRegistry.basis: Consequence-weighted synthetic cases, specialty domains, document stress cases, worst-cell gates, and reviewer rubrics.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Reviewed failures and corrections become quarantined regression cases after governance review.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires domain taxonomy, clinical reviewers, contamination controls, and consequence-aware scoring.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Supports model qualification, diligence services, and safer workflow expansion.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Synthetic and internal evaluation does not establish clinical validation or universal model superiority.

moatRegistry.name: Model qualification
moatRegistry.basis: Task-specific model passports, conformance evidence, worst-cell eligibility, canarying, and rollback controls.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Each qualified task cell expands portable routing evidence without granting authority to untested cells.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires model, provider, runtime, prompt, tool, privacy, and workflow evidence to remain version-bound.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Allows cost and quality optimization while preserving model independence.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: No model is approved for live PHI or high-risk clinical authority merely by registration.

moatRegistry.name: Workflow intelligence
moatRegistry.basis: Healthcare workflow maps, context packets, documentation gaps, outcome ledgers, and verified artifacts.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Each scoped pilot can add reusable workflow steps, evidence requirements, and failure modes.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Depends on healthcare process expertise, integration semantics, policy, and acceptance evidence.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not prove denial reduction, time savings, ROI, or customer outcomes before verified evidence.

moatRegistry.name: Connector policy layer
moatRegistry.basis: Capability-scoped connector manifests, official-API rules, read/write separation, terms review, and kill switches.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Validated connector policies and conformance receipts can be reused across governed workflows.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires legal, security, identity, data-rights, interoperability, and operational controls.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Supports protected integration pilots and future governed ecosystem distribution.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not imply live connector access, vendor approval, EHR writeback, or marketplace certification.

moatRegistry.name: Economic value telemetry
moatRegistry.basis: Cost per verified task, reviewer burden, correction burden, workflow value, and provenance-tagged outcome measures.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Verified pilot baselines improve pricing, capacity planning, model routing, and renewal evidence.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires trustworthy baselines, complete costs, acceptance evidence, and finance review.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Supports value-based pricing and capital-efficient model selection when evidence exists.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: No simulated or estimated value is a revenue, margin, savings, or ROI guarantee.

moatRegistry.name: Synthetic scenario library
moatRegistry.basis: No-PHI workflow cases, adversarial variants, buyer rehearsals, role-specific demos, and deterministic fixtures.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Each reviewed scenario expands test coverage, demos, evaluation, and pilot discovery without live data.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires domain-realistic cases, boundary coverage, deterministic outcomes, and claims-safe presentation.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Shortens assessment and pilot preparation while preserving no-PHI operation.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Synthetic demonstrations are not customer outcomes, clinical validation, or deployment evidence.

moatRegistry.name: Sovereign deployment controls
moatRegistry.basis: Assurance levels, enclave policies, residency, egress restrictions, capacity passports, and independent failover.
moatRegistry.compoundingMechanism: Validated regional and private deployment profiles improve reuse without collapsing jurisdictional controls.
moatRegistry.replicationFriction: Requires identity, cryptographic artifacts, private networking, capacity, recovery, and policy evidence.
moatRegistry.monetizationRelevance: Creates a path to private, regulated, and sovereign enterprise deployments after external approvals.
moatRegistry.blockedClaim: Does not establish sovereign certification, government authorization, regional compliance, or production deployment.

nextBestAction: Complete one buyer-specific Workflow Intelligence Assessment rehearsal with a baseline, acceptance rubric, reviewer burden, verified-intelligence-yield inputs, healthcare-value-returned inputs, and retained no-go boundary.
